title: Release a ratchet strap, lever held, handle folded flat
instruction: Release the strap so it goes slack, and let go.
context: Why: ratchet tie-downs are how most people strap a cooler or a box into a pickup bed or trailer, and every load that goes on has to come off. The knack: the handle frees the strap only when it is folded all the way over, flat, with its lock release held. Swung open without the release, it stops hard partway and looks fully open while the strap stays tight; let go before it is flat, and the cam that lifts the holding pawl pushes it back. The release is a sprung tab on the handle itself, so the hand that swings the handle has to keep it pulled through a half circle and push the last 20 degrees over the cam into the stop. The maker's steps: pull the lock release and rotate the main handle 180 degrees to lock it open; the spool is then free to turn and release the webbing. Unlike tasks that hold a button while pulling a handle straight out, one pinch keeps the release pulled through a half-turn, and the lock frees a load. Done by: anyone unloading a pickup, trailer or roof rack.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left), heights above the table top. Floor: a pickup-bed floor section, 19 mm (3/4 in) plywood with a 6 mm ribbed black rubber bed mat, 80 x 74 cm (x 10 to 90, y -34 to 40), screwed to the table (in the sim a free body of its real 12 kg). Track: two 610 mm (24 in) aluminium L-track sections, 32 mm wide and 10 mm tall, along x from x 15 to 76 at y -28.5 and y 26, each with a single-stud fitting and a 50 mm stainless O-ring standing up at x 30. Cooler: a Coleman Chiller 28 qt cooler with wheels, 508 mm long, 343 mm deep and 419 mm tall (HDPE shell, white lid), six 1 L water bottles inside (9.6 kg in all), lid shut, long side along x: from its front face at x 26.5 back to x 77.3, from y -13.5 (its right face) to y 20.8, wheels at its left end, free on the mat. Strap: a 1 in x 12 ft ratchet tie-down (Kinedyne 711281: 25 mm polyester webbing, vinyl-dipped wire hooks) centred on x 30: left hook on the left ring, over the lid, and down the right side, where from the lid's right edge the leg leans 23 deg out from vertical to the right ring, the ratchet on it. Ratchet: the strap's 1 in wide-handle ratchet (Kinedyne 800, zinc-plated steel, 59 mm wide, 41 mm high, 121 mm long, 0.34 kg); its spool axis points at the robot, along x, at x 30.0, y -21.0, z 26.5; the base lies on the leg, its short fixed strap running down to the right ring. Handle (0.12 kg): hinged on the spool axis, 100 mm from the axis to the grip's end, side plates 36 mm apart, a black vinyl grip bar 18 mm thick and 59 mm wide at its end; it turns from closed (0 deg, folded down the leg on the base) through outward to flat (180 deg, its hard stop, pointing up the leg) and stays where it is left (0.10 N m of friction). Release: a red sprung tab across the handle, 59 mm wide and 3 mm thick, its inner face 34 mm from the grip's end; it slides 8 mm toward the grip against a spring of 10 N at rest and 14 N fully pulled. With the release let go, the handle is held in its closed notch at 0 deg, and opened it stops at the crank stop at 115 deg; pulled 6 mm or more, it passes both. From 160 to 178 deg a cam lifting the base pawl pushes the handle back toward closed with 0.3 N m (about 3.5 N at the grip). At 178 deg or more with the release let go, the tab drops into the flat notch: the handle locks flat, both pawls are off the spool's 11 teeth and the strap goes slack. Folding the handle back with the release let go winds the spool one tooth (33 deg of handle) tighter. Start: the handle closed in its notch, the strap snug plus four clicks (200 N), both arms in their ready pose. One fixed layout, zero object jitter. Ratchet internals (spring, cam, stops) are estimates to measure on the bought unit.
scoring: Judged from the trial video and, at the end, a protractor or phone level, 2 N and 10 N spring scales and a steel rule. Locked flat: the handle within 3 deg of flat (in line with the base, 180 deg from closed), the release seated in the flat notch; on the real ratchet a 5 N push on the grip toward closed moves it less than 3 mm. Slack: a 2 N upward pull at the middle of the strap on the lid lifts it 30 mm or more (sim: the handle locked flat; the tension rule reads 0 and the leg is drawn slack). Clear and still: both grippers 30 mm or more from every part of the ratchet, and the handle turning less than 1 deg over the last 1 s. Past the crank stop: the handle opened to 125 deg or more at some point. Reached flat: the handle within 5 deg of flat at some point. Score 0, even if put back, if at any time the cooler moves more than 10 mm or tilts more than 5 deg from its start, or the strap is wound 2 or more teeth tighter than at the start (one tooth is allowed: a small forward push frees a stuck pawl). Otherwise, the first that fits: 1.0 locked flat, the strap slack, both grippers clear and the handle still; 0.75 locked flat and slack, but a gripper within 30 mm of the ratchet or the handle not still for 1 s; 0.5 the handle reached flat at some point but is not locked flat now (it sprang back or was folded back); 0.25 the handle got past the crank stop at some point but never reached flat, and is not locked flat; 0 anything else, including the untouched start, a handle opened only within its crank range (up to the 115 deg stop), or a strap wound tighter at the end than at the start and not locked flat. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The trial ends at the run limit or once 1.0 has held. Real-trial checks: the handle angle with the protractor (1 deg) and the 5 N push; slack with the 2 N scale and the rule (1 mm); teeth by the base pawl's clicks on the video or chalk marks on the spool's wound webbing; the cooler by tape marks at two corners of its base and a phone level on the lid.
run_limit: 1,200 steps (1 minute at 20 Hz); the scripted one-arm demo reaches full score in about 25 s (499 steps)
reset_notes: Nothing is used up. Hook both wire hooks on their stud rings, thread the running end through the spool slot, pull it hand-taut over the lid at x 30 cm, pump the handle until snug plus four clicks, then pull the release and fold the handle closed into its closed notch. Check: a 2 N pull at mid-lid lifts the strap less than 3 mm, and a 5 N push on the closed handle does not open it. Cooler back on its tape marks, lid shut, six 1 L bottles inside. Once a day calibrate the release spring (10 N scale on the tab) and the cam (10 N scale at the grip near flat). Run the simulator with -E object_jitter=0 (one fixed layout).
fidelity: Rigid bodies at product sizes; ratchet internals estimated. Webbing drawn, not cloth: a rule holds 200 N while the base pawl holds, 0 (drawn slack) once locked flat; base fixed on its strap (a real one rocks a few mm). Rules: crank stop 115 deg and closed notch freed by the release pulled 6 mm; cam 0.3 N m over 160-178 deg; flat lock at 178 deg, release let go; 1 tooth per 33 deg folded back unreleased. Tuned: release 10-14 N, weightless; handle friction 0.10 N m; bed a 12 kg free body.
